chapter: Reel 4: boyhood bands and the drummers he admired
title: Mr. Kirksey's school kids and the George McCaskel band
summary: A school-kid band from Booker T. Washington High with George Kelly and others replaced drummer Vincent Augberry with him.

bands.name: Hartley Toots and his Orange Pickers

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional

and wait for me until the end of the night and bring me home.

And I'll never forget the first song I ever played -- it was "Blue Prelude"; we played that, and we used to play "Dinah" and "Sweet Sue" and "One Sweet Letter from You" and all those types of tunes then.

So I stayed there, and there was a band -- I was still in school at the time, and there was a band with a bunch of school kids that was under the direction of Mr. Leander Kirksey, Kurtzin who was responsible for Nat Adderley and Cannonball Adderley, and he had just come out of college in Florida A&M, and he came down to Miami to teach at Booker Washington High School.

Well, he tried to organize a symphony orchestra there, a little symphony orchestra with the kids, and out of this, there was a band started by a fellow named George McCaskel, who was a saxophone player, and we used to play -- and he had the band at the Elks Rest with the school kids; George Kelly was in that band, and Ernest Thompson, who we nicknamed "Cocky" was on saxophone, and Sandy Williams was playing piano, and we had a trombone player there called "Footsie" -- he was the loudest thing you ever heard; and we had another trombone player there -- the guy's name was Pete Hastin Rose, but we called him "Pee Wee" because he was little -- about five feet five.

And the trumpet section, we had a fellow who I still
hear from now -- he's a minister, a big minister in Alabama, Arthur Duncan was one of the trumpet players. And there was Morris Meadows ...

And we had Palamiris -- he was the alto saxophone player; George McCaskel played alto and George Kelly played tenor. And the guitar player was George Tucker and I was -- well, before I came on there, the drummer was Vincent Augberry, who is still a very dear friend of mine now -- in New York, we hang out together.

But after playing at the barbecue stand for almost a year, and hearing the guys out there at the school talk about this band that was playing up at the Elk's Rest, and they heard about me playing at the barbecue stand, Vincent Augberry was leaving the band to go and join Hartley Toots as a front man, because he could dance and snake hip and all that stuff -- and plus he was a tall, handsome fellow, so he was going to front Hartley Toots. In other words, that was big time for him, so they asked me to join the band.

So I joined them, and we used to play all of the social society dances around Miami, because we worked a little bit cheaper than Hartley Toots did, so we used to get like, three or four social gigs a week.
